newsitem.title: USA: Clinton shocked, saddened by Hebron violence.
newsitem.headline: Clinton shocked, saddened by Hebron violence.

text.p: The White House on Wednesday expressed shock and sadness at an outbreak of violence in the West Bank town of Hebron at a time when sensitive negotiations over the town's fate were taking place.
A White House spokeswoman, Mary Ellen Glynn, said the United States was still hopeful Israel and the Palestinians would be able to reach an agreement on the handover of Hebron to Palestinian rule.
An off-duty Israeli soldier sprayed bullets at Arabs in a Hebron market on Wednesday, wounding eight in an attempt to sabotage a deal.

"We are shocked and saddened by what happened and it just underscores the need to bring about a peace agreement as soon as possible," Glynn told reporters travelling with President Bill Clinton on a vacation trip.

She said Clinton was aware of the situation and was receiving regular updates. She declined comment on reports that Clinton had invited Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to make a visit to Washington.
